title: NO KINGS Flag Day Rally – Rock Springs
description:
Rock Springs - The home of 56 nationalities is celebrating our diversity on Flag Day!

This is OUR flag and we're taking it back! 

Bring ANY flag that represents you! 
The red, white, and blue, or the LGBTQ! 

Design a flag or bring many! 
Show your spirit!
And Fly, Fly, them high!

For years Trump supporters have draped themselves in the Stars and Stripes, wielding the American flag as a weapon to question our loyalty, our values, and our love for this country. They branded themselves as the sole arbiters of patriotism, painting us as weak, un-American, or worse. We knew it was a lie—a hollow performance rooted in division, not unity. But we let it slide, and that was our mistake. No more. The flag belongs to all of us, and it’s time we took it back.

The flag, once a beacon of collective strength, was weaponized. It became a prop for warmongering, a badge of arrogance, and a litmus test for loyalty. For years, they’ve flown it over their rallies, their tax cuts for the rich, their assaults on civil liberties—all while accusing us of hating the very country we’ve fought to improve. 

But now, Trump supporters, in their fervor for a single man, have traded the American flag for a new one: a blue banner emblazoned with “Trump,” worshiping him as if her were a king! They’ve replaced the symbol of nearly 250 years of struggle, sacrifice, and aspiration with the name of a convicted felon. They’ve chosen a cult of personality over the principles of a nation. And in doing so, they’ve given us an opening—a chance to reclaim what was always ours.

Let them keep their blue Trump flags. Let them wave them at their rallies with their silly red hats, plaster them on their trucks, and fly them in their yards. That’s not our flag. Our flag is the one that flew over Valley Forge, that was raised on Iwo Jima, that draped the coffins of those who died for freedom. Our flag is the one that stood defiant after 9/11, not as a symbol of who we are today, but of who we strive to be.

It’s time to fly the Stars and Stripes again—not with arrogance, but with purpose. Fly it in the face of an administration that thrives on division, lies, and the erosion of the very liberties we hold dear. Fly it as a hat tip to the generations who laid down their lives so we could protest, vote, and speak freely today. Fly it for the millions who’ve marched, bled, and died to protect this nation from the kind of tyranny we now face at home.

This isn’t about nostalgia or blind allegiance. It’s about defiance. It’s about reminding ourselves and the world that America was founded on rebellion against autocrats, on the radical idea that power belongs to the people. Let them have their Trump flags. We’ll take back the red, white, and blue. We’ll fly it as a symbol of resistance, of resilience, of a patriotism that doesn’t divide but unites. We’ll fly it for the America we believe in—an America that belongs to all of us, not just the loudest or the most hateful. And when we do, we’ll show the world that the soul of this nation isn’t found in one man or one party. It’s found in us, in our defiance, in our hope, and in the flag we raise together. The citizens of the United States of America worship no kings!

# Solidarity With Marcy Rheintgen 
### Bartow, FL

This a local Indivisible event organized by Defund Oligarchy Blessed by Liberty.

We will have a short speech, a short march (less than .5 miles), and sign-wave on a main road. 

## Who is Marcy?
Marcy Rheintgen, 20-year-old college student, was arrested for entering a bathroom at the Florida State Capitol under an anti-trans bathroom law. 

## Why We Are Protesting?
We are protesting on this date in solidarity with Marcy's court date. These laws do not make restrooms safer for women and girls. Instead, these laws encourage dangerous people to judge everyone's bodies, putting all women and girls in a position where they need to prove their femininity and justify their self-expression. 

#### "I'm a cis/biological/assigned female at birth woman, why should I care?"
There are already cases of women being harassed because a customer or security guard thinks the woman doesn't look "girly" enough, making the woman show her driver's license, continuing to harass her because they believe the ID is fake. 

You or your friends may have short hair, wear baggy clothes, go out without makeup, wear suits instead of dresses, have body hair, or look strong instead of skinny. No one deserves to be targeted and treated with suspicion because of not fitting into someone else's idea of what feminine bodies, fashion, and hair should look like. 

#### "I'm still on the fence/uncomfortable/not sure"
We all have bladders. If you are out and about, everyone should be able to use the restroom in peace. Check yourself, are you uncomfortable because someone is doing something to you specifically, or are you bothered by someone minding their own business and just existing in a public space?

address_lines: Intersection of Little Rd and Citizens Dr

description:
On D-Day Anniversary, Pasco Resists Honors Veterans and Demands Protection of the VA

New Port Richey, FL — On the 81st anniversary of D-Day, Pasco Resists honors the sacrifice, bravery, and patriotism of American service members who fought on the beaches of Normandy to defend democracy and defeat fascism. A protest will take place on Friday June 6th from 4-6pm at the West Government Pasco Center, the intersection of Little Rd and Citizens Dr, (8731 Citizens Dr.)

“June 6 is a sacred date in our shared history,” said Doris Carroll, advocate, and leader with Pasco Resists. “It marks the moment when ordinary Americans did something extraordinary —risking everything to protect freedom not just for our nation, but for the world.”

The D-Day anniversary comes at a time when veterans face new battles at home. From underfunded healthcare to attempts to privatize and dismantle the VA, many veterans struggle to get the support they deserve after their service.

“Honoring our veterans means more than speeches—it means action,” said Carroll. “It means protecting the VA, expanding mental health care, and making sure no veteran is left behind.”

Pasco Resists is calling on elected officials and the public to recommit policies that truly honor the legacy of those who served. That includes rejecting VA budget cuts, improving access to healthcare, housing, and job opportunities, and standing against extremism in all forms.

“The men and women of D-Day didn’t fight to see their legacy used as a political prop,” Carroll added. “They fought for freedom, for equality, and for a better future. That’s the legacy we must live up to.”
________________________________________
About Pasco Resists
Pasco Resists is a grassroots organization based in Pasco County, Florida. We are dedicated to defending and uplifting veterans and working families through advocacy, education, and direct action. We believe a just society is one where every veteran receives the care, respect, and support they have earned.

title: An Evening with Former NC Rep. John Autry

location.venue: Special Events & Education Center @ Atrium Health Stanly

description:
## Hope in Times of Hopelessness

Former Representative John Autry of the North Carolina House will visit Albemarle to share reflections on his years of public service, what motivates him, and why it matters now more than ever. Most importantly, he’ll offer a call to action: whether it's a seat on the school board or in the state legislature.

### Join Indivisible Uwharrie and the Stanly County Democratic Women for this special evening of inspiration and engagement.

On December 31, 2024, John Autry retired from the North Carolina House of Representatives, concluding his service representing District 100 in Mecklenburg County.

Born and raised in Fayetteville, Autry graduated from Pine Forest High School in 1971 before moving to California to attend college. His studies were interrupted when he enlisted in the U.S. Navy, where he served honorably from 1972 to 1976 and was discharged with the rank of Petty Officer Third Class (E-4). After his military service, he returned to California State University, Fullerton, to complete his education.

Autry pursued a career in film production and returned to North Carolina in 1981 during a boom in the local film industry. Settling in Charlotte, he enjoyed a career spanning over 27 years as a cameraman, editor, producer, and director. In 1999, he directed a series of public service announcements for the local NBC affiliate. One of those spots, Tea Party, won the national Emmy Award for Best PSA of the Year.

After finishing second in the 2006 Democratic primary for U.S. Congress (NC-08), Autry was recruited to run for the Mecklenburg Soil & Water Conservation District Board of Supervisors, where he was re-elected in 2010. When the long-time incumbent for Charlotte City Council District 5 chose not to seek re-election, Autry was encouraged to run. He was elected in 2011 and re-elected twice before successfully running for the open seat in North Carolina House District 100, where he served four terms.

John Autry is married to Rebecca Wyndham. Together, they have four children and six grandchildren. John says being a grandparent is the one thing in life that truly isn’t overrated. Those six grandchildren, and the world he hopes to help shape for them, remain his greatest motivation for public service.

The Peace Vigil is hosted by Veterans for Peace and folks will gather along the sidewalk outside the library. The vigil is informal and consists of sign waving along with some socializing. Two objectives are to promote world peace and ending war . Your Tea & Talk host will be attending the vigil, and all are invited to join this separate event as well.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*
